newsitem.title: GERMANY: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest - May 9.
newsitem.headline: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest - May 9.

text.p: News from Reuters and the German press on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends

BERLIN - Berlin-based advertising agency Dorland says it has won the 40 million mark ($23.5 million) corporate image account of automaker Honda's German unit. Dorland, a unit of the Grey group, says the campaign will start in mid-June in print media and on television. The product account will stay with Bates Deutschland. (Reuter)

BERLIN - Bild Online, the website of tabloid newspaper Bild, has become one of the most popular online media in Germany. The site posted 2.9 million "hits" in April. The company in June will begin charging advertising customers based on the number of visits their ads tally on the website. (Die Welt)
MUNICH - Publishing group MagnaMedia Verlags AG says it will be disbanded and sold for 51 million marks to trade publishing group Weka. (Reuter)

DUESSELDORF - Retail group Kathreiner plans to close stores in over 300 locations, board spokesman Helmut Oxfart says in the Handelsblatt newspaper. Oxfart says retail group Spar Handels-AG has expressed interest in buying part of the Kathreiner company. (Reuter)

HAMBURG - Editor-in-chief of the weekly newspaper Die Zeit, Robert Leicht, will leave his position at the end of August, the publication's management says. Swiss journalist Roger de Weck will replace him. (Reuter)
FRANKFURT - Michael Grande will take charge of advertising, sales development, target group management, market research and the Miles & More division of airline Lufthansa. (Horizont)
WALLDORF - Bernd Weber will leave his post in public relations at brewing and beverage group Brau und Brunnen AG. (Kress)
WALLDORF - Arnold Kulbatzki will become deputy director of company communication at pay television channel Premiere, effective June 1. (Kress)
